host_prerequisites.not_adopted: The 2.9.8 and 2.9.13 pre-releases carried the fixes first and are not adopted. The 2.9.8 pre-release notes name PR 40519, which isolates distribution cgroups, and the 2.9.13 pre-release notes name PR 41512, which creates their namespaces. WSL 3.0.1 is the first stable release with both.
host_prerequisites.single_distribution: An install with a single systemd distribution, with no second systemd distribution running, has its own, lower install-only minimum: WSL 2.4.10 or later, the conservative figure among Microsoft's 2.4.4, Ubuntu's announcement of 2.4.8 and Ubuntu's install guide of 2.4.10. The recipe keeps the workstation's distribution running, so it adopts 3.0.1.
observations: The 2026-10-02 rehearsal on WSL 2.7.13 stopped at F1 on shared cgroups: that release has a shared cgroup tree, equal user uids collide, and a system-unit stop or restart can act on another distribution's processes.
The host was updated to WSL 3.0.1.0 on 2026-10-02 and passed its check (rootless container, interop, user manager).
Run 2 on 3.0.1.0 observed distinct cgroup namespaces, local process ids and two active user managers while both distributions ran.
host_prerequisites.gate: W1 records the version, and W5 must repeat the isolation proof before F1 changes anything.

host_prerequisites.title: Paired proof for two systemd distributions
host_prerequisites.requirement: The executable gate for two systemd distributions is the recipe's W5 paired record, not a version check. It takes five observations from both running distributions at once: the uid, the system state, the failed units, the user manager and the cgroup namespace. It passes by the rule the recipe page states in W5, together with the getty mask proof for the new distribution. A version check or one healthy user bus does not satisfy it.
host_prerequisites.receipt: The receipt records it in its paired_isolation object, one for the workstation and one for the new distribution, with the WSL version and kernel from W1 and the image revision from W2.

rehearsal.result: The paired record was observed on one host in rehearsals on throwaway distributions, and run 3 of 2026-10-02 passed it.
rehearsal.scope: A rehearsal is not acceptance of the real distribution.

host_prerequisites.gate: W5 of the recipe page, taken from both running distributions before F1.
